rule_title: Tests get equal effort; no vacuous / conditional assertions
message: test_cli_replay_forced_step_outputs_match_substitution wraps its key assertion in an `if` guard, so the test silently passes when the projection key is absent. This is an anti-test: a regression that drops the `dirty` field from the per-step JSON would make the test pass instead of fail.
evidence: tests/test_branch_io_and_cli.py: 'if "dirty" in by_id["step:2"]:\n            assert by_id["step:2"]["dirty"] is True'

rule_title: Tests get equal effort; assertions must be strict, not disjunctive
message: test_branch_names_uniqueness_and_count uses a logical OR to accept either sorted-order or a set match. The `or set(names) == {...}` clause is always satisfied for any 3-element subset of FACTS keys, so the sortedness check is effectively unenforced — a real anti-test pattern that lets reordering bugs slip through.
evidence: tests/test_parallel_branches.py: 'assert names == sorted(names) or set(names) == {f"research/{t}" for t in FACTS.keys()}'

rule_title: One coherent thematic improvement per round
message: The commit additionally bundles regenerated bytecode artifacts (.pyc files in tests/__pycache__/ and stepback/__pycache__/) into the round. These are not part of the test_forge thematic improvement and pollute the diff; tests/__pycache__ and stepback/__pycache__ should be gitignored.
evidence: git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat lists 8 binary .pyc files committed alongside the test changes

message: All new tests rely on synthesised in-test fixtures (_record_fixture / FakeOpenAI / FakeAnthropic / FakeLangchainTool / FakeMCPSession). For an agent_debugger_saas repo, a real-world recorded `.sb` fixture committed under tests/fixtures/ would harden the e2e-real-fixture requirement. The numeric thresholds added are valuable, but none of them exercise a previously-recorded on-disk artifact.
evidence: tests/ contains no fixtures/ directory with a checked-in .sb trace
